choices: My brother have a new job.
My brothers has a new job.
My brother having a new job.
My brother has a new job.
answer: My brother has a new job.
hints: Check the subject in each sentence. Is it one brother or more than one?
Start with the subject: "brother" means one person, and "brothers" means more than one.
One person or thing goes with has. Two or more go with have. A word ending in -ing cannot be the verb by itself. Check each sentence against these rules.

solution.methodName: Count the subject, then match the verb

steps.action: Look at the subject in each choice: "brother" is one person, and "brothers" is more than one.
One person takes "has". More than one takes "have".
steps.why: He, she, it and one person or thing go with has. We, they and two or more go with have.

steps.action: "My brother have" and "My brothers has" mix these up, so both are wrong.
"My brother having" has no full verb.
steps.why: A word ending in -ing needs a helper like is or was before it, as in "is having".

steps.action: The correct sentence is "My brother has a new job."

Brother is one person, so the verb must be has. Have goes with two or more, or with I and you.
Brothers means more than one, so the verb must be have. Has goes with only one person or thing.
This is not a full sentence. A word ending in -ing cannot be the verb by itself; it needs a helper like is.
